versioningRules: Requirement IDs are immutable and never reused, including after CANCELLED
Any change to a requirement's content creates version N+1; version N is kept unchanged in changeHistory

History is append-only; deleting or rewriting earlier versions is not permitted

requirements.title: Requirement registry with unique IDs and full schema

requirements.title: API Gateway: routing, versioning, correlation, CORS, security headers
requirements.description: Single entry point for all client traffic with routing, authentication, rate limiting, tracing and security headers.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Spring Cloud Gateway; routes /api/v1/<context>/**; JWT validation via identity-service JWKS (enabled in Phase 5); X-Correlation-Id generated if absent; access logging.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: /api/v1/{auth,users,restaurants,menu,cart,orders,payments,delivery,...}/** route to the owning service via discovery.
AC2: Protected routes without a valid JWT return 401 in the standard error format; public routes (register, login, OTP, public browse, payment webhook) are explicitly allow-listed.
AC3: Every response carries X-Correlation-Id and the same ID appears in downstream service logs.
AC4: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options and Referrer-Policy headers are present on all responses.
AC5: CORS allows only origins configured for the environment.
apiRequirements: Version prefix /api/v1; future breaking versions /api/v2 routed side by side
securityRequirements: Strip spoofable internal headers (e.g. X-User-Id) from inbound requests

requirements.title: Standard API contract: error format and OpenAPI documentation
requirements.description: Consistent error responses and complete OpenAPI documentation for every API.

requirements.title: Event backbone: versioned events, idempotent consumers, retry and DLT
requirements.description: Kafka-based asynchronous communication with a standard event envelope and reliable consumption.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Kafka (KRaft). Topic per aggregate (e.g. order.events.v1) keyed by aggregateId; envelope {eventId, eventType, eventVersion, occurredAt, producer, aggregateType, aggregateId, correlationId, causationId, payload}; consumer group per service; retry topics with backoff; <topic>.dlt.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Every event carries the standard envelope including eventId and eventVersion.
AC2: Re-delivering an already processed eventId has no additional effect (processed_events check).
AC3: Events for the same aggregate are consumed in production order.
AC4: A poison message moves to <topic>.dlt after the configured retries and raises an alert.
AC5: Schema changes within a major event version are backward compatible; breaking changes publish a new version.
testingRequirements: Testcontainers Kafka tests: duplicate delivery, ordering, DLT routing

requirements.title: Transactional outbox and idempotency keys
requirements.description: State changes and their events are committed atomically; mutating APIs are safe to retry.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Outbox table written in the same local transaction as the state change; relay publishes to Kafka. Idempotency-Key header stored with request hash and response.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: When Kafka is unavailable, state changes still commit and their events are published after recovery; no event is lost (failure test).
AC2: Order, payment, refund and wallet mutating endpoints require an Idempotency-Key.
AC3: A repeated request with the same key and payload returns the original response without re-executing.
AC4: The same key with a different payload returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
AC5: Idempotency records expire after a configurable TTL (PROPOSED default 24 h).

uiRequirements: Clients generate one key per user action and reuse it on retry
mobileRequirements: Same as web; keys persisted across app restarts for in-flight actions

requirements.title: Registration and login with JWT access token and rotating refresh token
requirements.description: Users register and log in; services authenticate requests with locally verifiable JWTs.
requirements.technicalRequirement: identity-service issues RS256 access tokens (PROPOSED 15 min) and opaque refresh tokens (PROPOSED 30 days) stored hashed with family-based reuse detection; JWKS endpoint for verification.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer registers with name, email and/or phone and password; a duplicate email/phone returns 409 USER_ALREADY_EXISTS.
AC2: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id or BCrypt; plaintext is never stored or logged.
AC3: Login returns an access token and a refresh token; invalid credentials return 401 without revealing which field was wrong.
AC4: Refresh rotates the refresh token; reusing a rotated token revokes the whole token family.
AC5: Downstream services validate access tokens via JWKS without calling identity-service per request.
databaseRequirements: identity_db: users (credentials), roles, permissions, user_roles, role_permissions, refresh_tokens
uiRequirements: Login and registration screens with client-side validation (React Hook Form + Zod)
securityRequirements: Web: access token in memory, refresh token in HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookie
Key rotation supported via JWKS kid
performanceRequirements: Login p95 < 500 ms excluding hashing cost tuning

requirements.title: RBAC with granular permissions and resource ownership checks
requirements.description: Access is controlled by role-mapped permissions plus ownership of the target resource, including brand and outlet scope for restaurant staff.

AC2: Permissions (e.g. ORDER_CREATE, ORDER_CANCEL, ORDER_VIEW, ORDER_REFUND, RESTAURANT_UPDATE, MENU_UPDATE, USER_BLOCK) are mapped to roles as data, not hard-coded per endpoint.
AC3: Each endpoint declares required permissions; a missing permission returns 403.
AC4: Customers access only their own orders; restaurant staff only their brand (HQ scope) or assigned outlets (outlet scope, REQ-OUTLET-002); partners only their assigned deliveries (IDOR tests).
AC5: Role/permission changes are audited and only SUPER_ADMIN can grant ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN.

requirements.title: Order state machine with guarded transitions and history
requirements.description: Order status is governed by an explicit state machine; invalid transitions are rejected.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Enum-based state machine in the domain model with one transition table per order type and role guards; optimistic locking on orders. Delivery table: docs/architecture/order-state-machine.md; in-store tables: ORDER_ARCHITECTURE.md (ROS design stage).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Delivery happy path: CREATED -> PAYMENT_PENDING -> CONFIRMED -> RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED -> PREPARING -> READY_FOR_PICKUP -> DELIVERY_ASSIGNED -> PICKED_UP -> OUT_FOR_DELIVERY -> DELIVERED -> COMPLETED (automatic). A partner assigned during preparation is recorded on the order immediately (deliveryPartnerId, partnerAssignedAt) and the order moves to DELIVERY_ASSIGNED automatically when it reaches READY_FOR_PICKUP.
AC7: If the assigned partner is released (unassigned), the order moves DELIVERY_ASSIGNED -> READY_FOR_PICKUP and reassignment starts.
AC2: Failure states PAYMENT_FAILED, RESTAURANT_REJECTED, CANCELLED, DELIVERY_FAILED, REFUND_PENDING, REFUNDED are reachable only from the states defined in the transition table.
AC3: Any other transition returns 409 INVALID_ORDER_TRANSITION.
AC4: Each transition is authorised by role (e.g. only restaurant staff for PREPARING, only assigned partner for PICKED_UP).
AC5: Every transition is stored in order_status_history (actor, timestamp, reason) and publishes the matching event.
AC6: Concurrent transitions on one order resolve via optimistic locking; exactly one succeeds.

AC8: In-store order types follow their own transition tables: dine-in and QR orders go to the kitchen with payment deferred and end SERVED -> COMPLETED when the table bill is settled; takeaway and pickup end HANDED_OVER -> COMPLETED (REQ-ORDER-008).
testingRequirements: Exhaustive transition table tests (valid and invalid)
Early-assignment test: partner assigned in PREPARING, order auto-moves to DELIVERY_ASSIGNED on READY_FOR_PICKUP

AC6: Acceptance generates one KOT per kitchen station (REQ-KOT-002).

requirements.title: Customer order cancellation
requirements.description: Customers can cancel before the restaurant starts preparing; paid orders are refunded.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Cancel command validated against state; triggers refund saga step, coupon release and delivery unassignment.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer can cancel in CREATED, PAYMENT_PENDING, CONFIRMED or RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED.
AC2: Customer cancellation in PREPARING or later returns 409 ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE.
AC3: SUPPORT_AGENT/ADMIN may cancel in later states with a mandatory reason; the action is audited.
AC4: Cancelling a paid order moves it through REFUND_PENDING to REFUNDED via payment-service.
AC5: Cancellation releases the coupon reservation and any delivery assignment.
uiRequirements: Cancel button visible only in cancellable states with confirmation

requirements.title: Order saga orchestration with timeouts and compensation
requirements.description: order-service orchestrates payment, restaurant acceptance and delivery assignment, compensating on failure.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Orchestrated saga driven by events and the state machine; saga timeouts via scheduled jobs; no distributed (XA) transactions.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: The saga reacts to PaymentCompleted/PaymentFailed, RestaurantAccepted/Rejected, DeliveryAssigned/AssignmentFailed events.
AC2: An order in PAYMENT_PENDING longer than 15 minutes (PROPOSED) moves to PAYMENT_FAILED and is closed.
AC3: Compensations: refund payment, release coupon, unassign partner, restore stock.
AC4: Failure tests prove consistent end states for payment failure, restaurant rejection, no partner available and a service crash mid-saga.
databaseRequirements: order_db: saga_state (or columns on orders) with deadlines

requirements.title: Order history and details
requirements.description: Customers, restaurants and operators view orders appropriate to their role.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Paginated queries with indexes on (user_id, created_at), (branch_id, status, created_at).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Customers see paginated order history and order detail with status timeline.
AC2: Restaurant staff list orders by status and date for their branches.
AC3: Admin/support search orders by order ID, user, restaurant and date range.

requirements.title: Online payment initiation via gateway abstraction
requirements.description: Customers pay for orders by UPI, card (and net banking via the gateway); amounts come from the order, never the client.
requirements.technicalRequirement: PaymentGateway port with provider adapter (OQ-03) and a mock adapter for dev/test; gateway-hosted checkout keeps card data out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Creating a payment uses the order's server-side amount; any client-supplied amount is ignored.
AC2: Supported methods: UPI and card; net banking where the gateway supports it.
AC3: Payment states: INITIATED -> PROCESSING -> SUCCESS | FAILED (refund states in REQ-PAYMENT-005).
AC4: The platform never receives or stores raw card numbers or CVV.
AC5: A mock gateway adapter supports success, failure, delay and duplicate-webhook scenarios for tests.
uiRequirements: Payment method selection; gateway checkout handoff
mobileRequirements: UPI intent / gateway SDK flow where applicable

requirements.title: Payment webhook processing with signature verification
requirements.description: Payment status changes only from verified gateway webhooks or server-side status checks.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Public webhook route through gateway; HMAC signature verification; dedupe by gateway event ID; monotonic state updates; outbox events.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Webhooks with an invalid signature return 401, change nothing and raise a security alert.
AC2: Duplicate webhooks are processed exactly once (dedupe by gateway event ID).
AC3: Out-of-order webhooks never regress state (SUCCESS is not overwritten by PROCESSING).
AC4: Client-reported payment results never change payment state.
AC5: SUCCESS publishes PaymentCompleted; FAILED publishes PaymentFailed.
uiRequirements: Payment result page polls/subscribes for server-confirmed status
performanceRequirements: Webhook acknowledged < 2 s (process asynchronously if needed)

requirements.title: Payment reconciliation and retry
requirements.description: Stuck payments are reconciled with the gateway and failed payments can be retried.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Scheduled reconciliation job using gateway status API; new payment_transaction per attempt; daily settlement report.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Payments in PROCESSING longer than 10 minutes (PROPOSED) are resolved via the gateway status API.
AC2: A customer can retry a failed payment for the same order within the payment window; each attempt is a new transaction record.
AC3: A daily reconciliation report compares gateway records with internal records and flags mismatches.
uiRequirements: Retry payment action on failed payment screen
testingRequirements: Reconciliation job tests with mock gateway

requirements.title: Cash on Delivery
requirements.description: Customers can pay cash on delivery where enabled.
requirements.technicalRequirement: COD eligibility rules (city, restaurant, max amount) in payment-service; collection confirmed by partner action.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: COD is offered only when enabled for the city/restaurant and the order total is within the configured limit (PROPOSED).
AC2: COD orders are confirmed without online payment.
AC3: On delivery the partner confirms cash collected; the payment becomes COLLECTED and the amount is recorded against the partner.

requirements.title: Full and partial refunds
requirements.description: Refunds are issued automatically on cancellation/rejection or manually by authorised staff.
requirements.technicalRequirement: refunds table; gateway refund API or wallet credit; refund webhooks; RefundCreated/RefundCompleted events; audit.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Full and partial refunds go to the original method or to the wallet.
AC2: The sum of refunds never exceeds the captured amount.
AC3: Manual refunds require ORDER_REFUND permission and a reason; automatic refunds run on cancellation/rejection.
AC4: Refund lifecycle REFUND_PENDING -> REFUNDED | REFUND_FAILED is confirmed by gateway webhook.
AC5: Every refund is audited with actor, amount and reason.
uiRequirements: Admin/support refund dialog; customer refund status

requirements.title: Customer wallet ledger and wallet payment
requirements.description: Each customer has a wallet whose balance changes only through immutable ledger entries.
requirements.technicalRequirement: wallets + wallet_transactions in payment-service; balance updates with optimistic locking; funding sources limited per OQ-13.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Each customer has one wallet; balance changes only through wallet_transactions (CREDIT/DEBIT with reference type and ID).
AC2: Balance can never go negative; concurrent debits are safe (concurrency test).
AC3: A wallet with sufficient balance can pay an order in full; refunds and cashback can be credited to it.
AC4: Sum of transactions always equals the balance (reconciliation check).
uiRequirements: Wallet screen with balance and history

requirements.title: Split payment (wallet + gateway)
requirements.description: Customers apply part of their wallet balance and pay the remainder through the gateway.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Wallet hold + gateway payment within the order saga; release hold on gateway failure.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer can apply a partial wallet amount and pay the rest via gateway.
AC2: If the gateway payment fails, the wallet hold is released automatically.
AC3: Refunds of split payments are apportioned to wallet and original method proportionally (PROPOSED).

statusHistory.reason: STEP 1 requirement analysis; P2 backlog pending product confirmation

requirements.title: Delivery partner onboarding and profile
requirements.description: Partners sign up, submit documents and become active after admin verification.
requirements.technicalRequirement: delivery-service owns delivery_partners; documents through media-service private storage.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A partner signs up and submits ID proof, driving licence (if motorised) and vehicle type.
AC2: Admin verifies and activates or rejects with reason; actions are audited.
AC3: Profile includes name, phone, vehicle, zone, rating and capacity (max concurrent orders, PROPOSED default 1).
AC4: Only verified ACTIVE partners can go online.
mobileRequirements: Partner signup with camera document capture

requirements.title: Partner availability states
requirements.description: Partners move between OFFLINE, ONLINE, BUSY, ON_BREAK and DISABLED.
requirements.technicalRequirement: State machine in delivery-service; availability index in Redis; stale-location detection from location-service.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: States OFFLINE, ONLINE, BUSY, ON_BREAK, DISABLED (REF p.9) with a defined transition table.
AC2: Going ONLINE requires a location update newer than 60 seconds (PROPOSED).
AC3: A partner without location updates for 2 minutes (PROPOSED) is marked stale and excluded from assignment.
AC4: DISABLED can be set only by ADMIN.

requirements.title: Delivery assignment engine with scoring
requirements.description: The engine selects the most suitable partner using a documented, configurable scoring model.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Candidate search via Redis GEO (GEOSEARCH); hard filters then weighted score; offer with timeout; distributed lock per order; decision log.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Assignment starts on RESTAURANT_ACCEPTED, timed so the partner's ETA to the restaurant approximates remaining preparation time; it starts immediately at READY_FOR_PICKUP if not yet assigned.
AC2: Hard filters: ONLINE, verified, below capacity, not stale, within search radius (start 2 km, expand to 5 km per REF p.9).
AC3: Score = weighted sum of normalised distance, ETA, workload/availability, rating and acceptance rate; weights configurable (defaults 40/20/10/20/10 per REF p.9).
AC4: Offers expire after 30 seconds (REF p.9); on reject/timeout the next candidate is offered; a partner never receives the same order twice.
AC5: Exactly one partner is assigned per order under concurrency; DeliveryAssigned is published.
AC6: If no partner accepts within the maximum radius/attempts, AssignmentFailed is published and ops are alerted.
AC7: Candidate scores and the decision are logged for explainability.
mobileRequirements: Offer card with countdown and accept/reject
performanceRequirements: Time to first offer p95 < 5 s (PROPOSED)

requirements.title: Delivery workflow and navigation
requirements.description: Assigned partners navigate, pick up and deliver orders, or report delivery failure.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Partner commands in delivery-service publish OrderPickedUp/OutForDelivery/OrderDelivered/DeliveryFailed consumed by order-service.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: The assigned partner sees restaurant and customer details needed for the delivery only.
AC2: Navigation opens the device maps app via deep link to restaurant and then customer.
AC3: The partner marks PICKED_UP, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY and DELIVERED; each updates the order state via events.
AC4: The partner can report DELIVERY_FAILED with a reason category; support is notified.
securityRequirements: Customer PII hidden after delivery completes

requirements.title: Partner earnings and delivery history
requirements.description: Partners view per-delivery earnings, totals and history.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Earnings computed on OrderDelivered with a configurable rule; payout/settlement out of scope pending OQ-12.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Each delivered order creates an earnings record using the configured rule (e.g. base + per-km).
AC2: Partners see daily and weekly totals and paginated delivery history.
AC3: COD cash collected is shown separately from earnings.

requirements.title: Delivery partner location ingestion
requirements.description: Partner apps stream location; the latest position is queryable in real time and history is retained.
requirements.technicalRequirement: location-service validates updates, writes latest to Redis GEO, publishes to Kafka (key = partnerId) and batch-persists history to partitioned PostgreSQL tables.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: While ONLINE, the app sends latitude, longitude, accuracy, speed, heading and timestamp every 5-10 seconds.
AC2: Updates with invalid coordinates, stale timestamps or implausible speed (GPS drift/spoofing heuristic) are dropped and counted.
AC3: The latest location is stored in Redis GEO; history is persisted asynchronously in batches, partitioned by day, retained 90 days (PROPOSED).
AC4: The ingestion request path never waits on a database write.
AC5: Offline partners show 'last seen'; queued updates sent after reconnect are accepted if not older than 5 minutes (PROPOSED).
securityRequirements: Partner can only post own location
performanceRequirements: Design target 100K updates/s at full scale (NFR-SCALE-002)

requirements.title: Distance calculation and delivery serviceability
requirements.description: The platform computes distances between restaurant, customer and partner and decides serviceability. Pulled forward to Phase 7 because cart delivery-fee pricing needs it.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Phase 7: shared geo library (Haversine distance x configurable road factor, radius check). Phase 10: exposed by location-service; RoutingProvider port for a routing API later (OQ-05).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Distances are computed for restaurant->customer, partner->restaurant and partner->customer.
AC2: An address is serviceable only if within the branch's delivery radius.
AC3: Swapping to a routing provider requires no API change for callers.
testingRequirements: Distance accuracy tests against known coordinates

requirements.title: Estimated delivery time (ETA)
requirements.description: ETA is shown during discovery, checkout and tracking, and its accuracy is measured.
requirements.technicalRequirement: ETA = remaining preparation time + partner->restaurant travel + restaurant->customer travel + buffer; speed profile configurable per city/time; ML later.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: ETA is computed with the documented formula and exposed at discovery, checkout and tracking.
AC2: ETA is recalculated on every status change and every 30 seconds during active delivery (PROPOSED).
AC3: Predicted vs actual delivery time is recorded and exported as an accuracy metric.

requirements.title: Real-time WebSocket infrastructure with authenticated subscriptions
requirements.description: Clients receive server push over WebSocket with secure, horizontally scalable delivery.
requirements.technicalRequirement: realtime-service: Spring WebSocket + STOMP; JWT on CONNECT; subscription authorisation; cross-instance fan-out via Redis Pub/Sub; consumes Kafka events.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: STOMP CONNECT requires a valid JWT; unauthenticated connections are refused.
AC2: Subscriptions are authorised: customers to their own orders, staff to their branches, partners to their assignments.
AC3: A message reaches the user regardless of which realtime-service instance holds the connection.
AC4: Clients reconnect with backoff, resync state via REST, and fall back to polling if WebSocket is unavailable.
AC5: Heartbeats detect and close dead connections.
apiRequirements: WS /ws (STOMP); destinations documented in event design
securityRequirements: Token expiry enforced on long-lived connections

requirements.title: Real-time order, payment and notification updates
requirements.description: Customers, restaurants and partners see status changes without manual refresh.
requirements.technicalRequirement: realtime-service maps order, payment, delivery, notification, kitchen and table events to user, branch, station and table-session destinations.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Customers receive order and payment status changes within 2 seconds of the event (PROPOSED).
AC2: The restaurant live orders screen shows new and updated orders without manual refresh.
AC3: Partners receive offers and assignment changes in real time.
AC4: In-app notifications are pushed to connected clients.

requirements.title: Live delivery partner tracking for customers
requirements.description: During an active delivery the customer sees the partner on a map with live ETA.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: From partner assignment (DeliveryAssigned event, which can precede the DELIVERY_ASSIGNED order status) until DELIVERED, the customer sees the partner's location updated every 5-10 seconds.

requirements.title: Event-driven multi-channel notifications
requirements.description: Domain events trigger templated notifications over push, SMS, email and in-app channels.
requirements.technicalRequirement: notification-service consumes events, resolves recipients/devices, renders versioned templates, dispatches via provider adapters (fake adapters locally).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Order lifecycle events map to notifications as in REF p.11 (e.g. Order Placed -> 'Order confirmed' push + in-app).
AC2: Provider adapters exist behind interfaces: push (FCM/APNs), SMS, email; local environment uses fake/mail-catcher adapters.
AC3: Templates are versioned and support variables and locale.
AC4: OTP and other transactional SMS are sent on a priority path.

mobileRequirements: Push handling with deep link to order
securityRequirements: No sensitive data in push payloads

requirements.title: In-app notification centre
requirements.description: Users browse notifications and manage read state.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Per-user notification inbox in notification_db with retention job.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Users list notifications (paginated), mark one or all as read and see an unread count.
AC2: Notifications are retained for 90 days (PROPOSED).
uiRequirements: Bell icon with badge; notification list

requirements.title: Notification reliability, deduplication and preferences
requirements.description: Notifications are retried, deduplicated, routed to fallbacks and respect user preferences.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Retry topics with exponential backoff; DLQ; dedupe key; per-user channel preferences.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Failed sends retry with exponential backoff; permanent failures go to a DLQ.
AC2: Critical messages fall back to an alternative channel (e.g. push failure -> SMS).
AC3: Deduplication key (orderId + status + channel) prevents duplicate notifications.
AC4: Users can opt out of marketing per channel; transactional and OTP messages cannot be disabled.
AC5: Delivery status (sent, delivered, failed) is tracked and exported as metrics.

requirements.title: Ratings and reviews for delivered orders
requirements.description: Customers rate and review the restaurant, delivery and products after delivery.
requirements.technicalRequirement: review-service verifies order eligibility via OrderDelivered read model; ReviewCreated event.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Only the customer of a DELIVERED order can review it; one review per order, editable for 7 days (PROPOSED).
AC2: Ratings 1-5 for restaurant and delivery, optional per product; optional text and images.
AC3: Submitting a review publishes ReviewCreated.
databaseRequirements: review_db: reviews, ratings, restaurant_reviews, product_reviews, review_images
uiRequirements: Rate order prompt after delivery; reviews list

requirements.title: Rating aggregation, restaurant replies and moderation
requirements.description: Ratings are aggregated for display; restaurants reply; admins moderate abusive content.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Aggregates maintained incrementally; RatingAggregated event consumed by search and restaurant services.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Restaurant and product average rating and count update after each review and appear in search and detail pages.
AC2: A restaurant can post one reply per review.
AC3: ADMIN/SUPPORT can hide a review with a reason (audited); hidden reviews are excluded from aggregates.
uiRequirements: Reviews screen in restaurant dashboard; moderation list in admin

requirements.title: Rule-based recommendations
requirements.description: Customers receive explainable recommendations based on history, preferences and context.
requirements.technicalRequirement: recommendation-service builds a read model from OrderDelivered, ReviewCreated, UserPreferencesUpdated events and scores candidates from search-service.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Signals: previous orders, cuisine preference, price range, time of day, location, restaurant popularity, ratings.
AC2: Only open and serviceable restaurants/products are recommended.
AC3: Each item includes a reason code (e.g. ORDERED_BEFORE, POPULAR_NEARBY, MATCHES_PREFERENCE).
AC4: New users get popular-nearby recommendations (cold start).
securityRequirements: Personal signals visible only to the user

requirements.title: ML/LLM-ready recommendation strategy interface
requirements.description: Recommendation strategies can be replaced by ML/LLM models and A/B tested.
requirements.technicalRequirement: RecommendationStrategy interface; experiment bucketing; offline evaluation pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Strategies are pluggable without API changes.
AC2: Users can be bucketed into experiments; CTR and conversion are measured per strategy.
AC3: A model is rolled out only after offline metrics meet an agreed threshold.

requirements.title: AI food assistant: natural language to structured search criteria
requirements.description: Customers describe what they want in natural language; the assistant converts it to validated criteria and returns real results.
requirements.technicalRequirement: ai-service uses LLM structured output constrained by a JSON schema; results always come from search/recommendation tools.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: 'I want spicy vegetarian food under 300 rupees' produces {diet: VEGETARIAN, spice: HIGH, maxPrice: 300} that validates against the criteria schema.
AC2: Ambiguous or unsupported requests produce a clarifying question instead of guessed criteria.
AC3: Every restaurant, dish and price in a response exists in tool results for that turn (no fabricated items; verified by evaluation set).
AC4: Conversation context is kept within a session.
uiRequirements: Chat panel with result cards and quick add-to-cart
mobileRequirements: Chat screen; voice input optional later
testingRequirements: Golden evaluation set for criteria extraction

requirements.title: Controlled tool execution (no direct database access)
requirements.description: The LLM can act only through a registry of tools that call backend APIs with the user's permissions.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Tool registry in ai-service; tools call public APIs through the gateway using the caller's token; schema-validated inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Only registered tools can be invoked (initially searchFood, getMenu, getRecommendations, addToCart, getOrderStatus).
AC2: Tools call backend APIs through the gateway with the end user's permissions; ai-service has no database credentials for other services.
AC3: Tool inputs are schema-validated; invalid tool calls are rejected and logged.
AC4: State-changing tools (e.g. addToCart) require explicit user confirmation in the UI.
AC5: Every tool call is logged with traceId, tool name and outcome.
securityRequirements: Least privilege; no order placement or payment tools in v1

requirements.title: AI guardrails, cost control and monitoring
requirements.description: The assistant resists prompt injection, minimises data sharing, controls cost and is observable.
requirements.technicalRequirement: System prompt isolation, output validation, red-team suite, PII minimisation, per-user rate limits, budget tracking, keyword-search fallback; metrics to Prometheus.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A prompt-injection red-team test set runs in CI; no test can trigger a non-registered tool or reveal system instructions.
AC2: Only data needed for the request is sent to the LLM provider; payment data and contact details are never sent.
AC3: Per-user rate limits and a monthly cost budget are enforced; on provider failure or budget exhaustion the assistant falls back to keyword search.
AC4: Admin dashboard shows AI latency, token usage, cost, error rate and tool call distribution.

requirements.title: Media upload and delivery via object storage
requirements.description: Images and documents are stored in object storage; the database holds only metadata.
requirements.technicalRequirement: media-service issues pre-signed upload URLs (S3-compatible; MinIO locally), validates, scans, generates image variants, serves public images via CDN and private files via short-lived signed URLs.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Clients upload directly to object storage with pre-signed URLs; PostgreSQL stores only metadata.
AC2: Content type, extension and magic bytes are validated; size limits 5 MB for images and 10 MB for documents (PROPOSED).
AC3: Files pass a malware-scan hook before becoming visible.
AC4: Images are resized to standard variants and served via CDN.
AC5: Private documents (restaurant/partner KYC) are accessible only to the owner and admins via signed URLs expiring within 5 minutes (PROPOSED).
uiRequirements: Upload component with progress and validation errors
testingRequirements: File upload security tests (polyglot, oversized, wrong type)
securityRequirements: No public bucket listing; private bucket for documents

requirements.title: Administer users, restaurants and delivery partners
requirements.description: Admins search, review, approve, block and unblock platform participants.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Admin endpoints live in owning services; admin-service aggregates views where needed; all actions audited.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Admins list, search and filter users, restaurants and partners and view details.
AC2: Admins approve/reject restaurants and partners and block/unblock users (USER_BLOCK); blocking revokes all sessions.
AC3: Every admin action requires the relevant permission and is audited.

requirements.title: Order, payment, refund and coupon oversight
requirements.description: Admins investigate orders and payments, issue refunds and manage coupons.
requirements.technicalRequirement: admin-service aggregates order timeline (order, payment, delivery events) for a single view.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Admins search orders and payments and see a unified timeline across order, payment and delivery.
AC2: Admins issue full/partial refunds with reason; refunds above a threshold need SUPER_ADMIN approval (PROPOSED).
AC3: Admins manage platform coupons (REQ-PROMO-001).

requirements.title: Complaints and customer support
requirements.description: Customers raise complaints about orders; support agents triage and resolve them.
requirements.technicalRequirement: admin-service owns complaints (support tickets) with SLA timers.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: A customer can raise a complaint on an order with category, description and images.
AC2: Support agents assign, respond to and resolve complaints; statuses OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CLOSED.
AC3: Support agents can issue refunds within their permission limits.
AC4: SLA timers flag overdue complaints.

requirements.title: Engineering, system health and audit visibility in admin
requirements.description: Admins see requirement, development, test, deployment and production status, releases, system health, AI monitoring and audit logs.

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: For each requirement the admin sees requirement status, development status, test status, deployment status and production status.
AC2: Release list shows notes, status and evidence links.
AC3: System health panel shows service status and key metrics; AI monitoring panel per REQ-AI-003.
AC4: Audit log viewer supports filtering by actor, action, entity and date.
uiRequirements: Admin Requirements, Releases, System Health, AI Monitoring, Audit Logs screens

requirements.title: Business analytics and reports
requirements.description: Platform and restaurant KPIs are computed from events, never from operational databases.
requirements.technicalRequirement: analytics-service consumes domain events into analytics_db (partitioned PostgreSQL initially; warehouse later).
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: KPIs: orders, GMV, average order value, cancellation rate, payment failure rate, average delivery time, ETA accuracy, coupon usage.
AC2: Admin reports filter by date, city and restaurant and export to CSV.
AC3: Restaurant analytics: orders, revenue, top items, ratings, preparation time.
AC4: Analytics queries never run against operational service databases.
databaseRequirements: analytics_db: fact_orders, fact_payments, fact_deliveries, daily aggregates
uiRequirements: Admin reports; restaurant analytics dashboard with charts
securityRequirements: Restaurant sees only its own analytics
performanceRequirements: Report queries p95 < 2 s for 90-day range (PROPOSED)

requirements.title: Audit trail for sensitive operations
requirements.description: Every sensitive operation produces an immutable audit record.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Services emit AuditEvent via outbox in the same transaction; audit-service stores append-only records with hash chaining.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Refunds, user blocking, restaurant approval, price changes, role changes, permission changes and admin actions produce audit records.
AC2: Records contain actor, actor role, action, entity type and ID, old value, new value, timestamp, IP (where appropriate) and traceId.
AC3: The audit store has no update/delete API; records are hash-chained so tampering is detectable (PROPOSED).
AC4: A sensitive operation cannot commit without its audit event (same-transaction outbox).
AC5: Admins can search audit records; retention period per OQ-20.
testingRequirements: One audit test per sensitive operation
securityRequirements: Audit values mask secrets and full card/phone data

requirements.title: Shared design system for web and mobile
requirements.description: Centralised tokens and components give web and mobile a consistent look while respecting platform UX.
requirements.technicalRequirement: web/packages/ui: design tokens (Tailwind preset + CSS variables), React components, component catalogue with visual baselines.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Colours, typography, spacing, radius and shadows are defined once and consumed by all web and mobile apps.
AC2: Components: button, input, card, modal, toast, table, navigation, form controls, loading, empty and error states, each with documented variants.
AC3: Components meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard accessibility (NFR-A11Y-001).
AC4: A component catalogue (e.g. Storybook) has visual regression baselines.
mobileRequirements: Platform variants (e.g. bottom sheets, safe areas, touch targets >= 44px)

requirements.title: Customer web application
requirements.description: Responsive React web app covering the full customer journey.
requirements.technicalRequirement: React + TypeScript + Vite, React Router, TanStack Query, Axios (generated client), Zustand, React Hook Form + Zod, Tailwind CSS.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Implements login, registration, location selection, discovery, search, filters, restaurant details, menu, product details, cart, coupon, address, checkout, payment, order tracking, order history, reviews, profile, wallet, notifications, favourites and recommendations (each backed by its module requirement).
AC2: Layout is responsive from 360 px width to desktop.

requirements.title: Server-side bill computation
requirements.description: Grand total = subtotal − discounts − coupon + packaging + service charge + delivery fee + tax ± round-off. The exact order of applying discounts before or after tax is fixed in design and documented, per tax rules.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Owner: pos-service (billing module) with payment-service. Full specification: docs/requirements/restaurant-os/BILLING_REQUIREMENTS.md (REQ-BILL-001); design in the ROS design stage.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Grand total = subtotal − discounts − coupon + packaging + service charge + delivery fee + tax ± round-off. The exact order of applying discounts before or after tax is fixed in design and documented, per tax rules.
AC2: Tax is calculated per line from the line's tax class (inclusive or exclusive), with a per-rate tax summary on the bill.
AC3: Round-off to the nearest rupee is configurable per outlet and shown as its own line.
AC4: All amounts are `BigDecimal` with HALF_UP. The calculation shares one pricing library with cart-service, so online and in-store totals follow the same rules.
AC5: Client-sent totals are never trusted. The server recalculates on every change.

requirements.title: Automatic, idempotent consumption on order completion
requirements.description: On `OrderCompleted` (ROS-OQ-09), each line's recipe version (REQ-RECIPE-002 AC2), including add-ons and combo slots (REQ-RECIPE-005), is expanded into ingredient quantities × order quantity. Example: 2 Paneer Pizza → Paneer −200 g, Cheese −160 g, Sauce −100 ml.
requirements.technicalRequirement: Owner: inventory-service. Full specification: docs/requirements/restaurant-os/INVENTORY_REQUIREMENTS.md (REQ-INV-004); design in the ROS design stage.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: On `OrderCompleted` (ROS-OQ-09), each line's recipe version (REQ-RECIPE-002 AC2), including add-ons and combo slots (REQ-RECIPE-005), is expanded into ingredient quantities × order quantity. Example: 2 Paneer Pizza → Paneer −200 g, Cheese −160 g, Sauce −100 ml.
AC2: Consumption is idempotent. A unique key on (order ID, order line ID, recipe version) means a duplicate or replayed event never deducts twice (ROS §15). There is a test that replays the event.
AC3: Lines without a recipe post nothing and are listed in a "products without recipes" report.
AC4: `InventoryConsumed` is published with the order ID and the movements.
AC5: Orders cancelled after preparation post waste instead (REQ-INV-008, ROS-OQ-09).
